quiz.q: The function check(age) raises ValueError('age cannot be negative') when age is below 0, and otherwise returns age. What is the last line Python prints for check(-3) when nobody handles the exception?
rationales: The traceback ends with the exception's type and message, not the function's name and argument.
The raise statement stops check before the return statement.

quiz.q: A person types abc when the program asks for their age. Which instrument fits?
options: if / raise, and handle the exception
rationales: Under python -O the assert would not run, and this is an error of the user, not of the programmer.
A log message records the event; it does not decide what the program does about it.

quiz.q: Under python -O, what happens to the statement  assert False, 'boom'?
options: It is removed, so nothing happens
rationales: Optimisation removes assert statements, so nothing is raised.
The syntax is valid; the statement is simply not compiled.

quiz.q: A program never calls basicConfig. It runs logging.debug('a'), logging.info('b'), logging.warning('c'). What appears?
rationales: The default threshold is WARNING, so the debug and info calls are dropped.
The warning call is at the threshold, so it is shown, on standard error.

quiz.q: What is the number of the level logging.ERROR?
rationales: 30 is WARNING.
50 is CRITICAL.

quiz.q: The program calls logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) and then logging.critical('x'). What happens?
rationales: disable(CRITICAL) silences CRITICAL and everything below it.
Disabled messages are dropped without an error.

quiz.q: basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) is called, then basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG), then logging.debug('x'). What is shown?
options: Nothing: the second call is ignored
rationales: The second call changed nothing, so the threshold is still INFO.
basicConfig does not complain; unless force=True is passed it simply does nothing.

quiz.q: With the level at INFO, log.debug('v %s', obj) and log.debug(f'v {obj}') are called. When is obj converted to text?
rationales: The call with an argument formats only when the message is emitted.
The f-string builds its text before the call, whether or not the message is shown.

quiz.q: Which control runs a called function at full speed without stopping inside it?
rationales: Step In goes inside the call.
Step Out finishes the current function; it does not skip a call on the next line.

quiz.q: The debugger is stopped on a line inside add, and you want to be back in the caller. Which control?
rationales: Continue runs to the next breakpoint, which may be far away.
Step In would go deeper, not back.

quiz.q: factorial(3) loops over range(n + 1) and multiplies total, starting at 1, by i. What does it return?
rationales: 6 needs the loop to start at 1; range(n + 1) starts at 0.
Multiplying by 0 is not an error; it makes total 0 on the first pass.
